	<item>
		<title>See Peter Marlow&#8217;s &#8216;The English Cathedral&#8217; at London&#8217;s Oldest Gothic Church</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/peter-marlow-english-cathedral-architecture-exhibition/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Wed, 15 Jul 2026 17:59:12 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[History]]></category>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-2.jpg" alt="See Peter Marlow&#8217;s &#8216;The English Cathedral&#8217; at London&#8217;s Oldest Gothic Church" />Between 2010 and 2011, Marlow documented all 42 Anglican cathedrals across the breadth and length of England.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? ]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-2.jpg" alt="See Peter Marlow&#8217;s &#8216;The English Cathedral&#8217; at London&#8217;s Oldest Gothic Church" />


<p>Acclaimed British photographer <a href="https://www.magnumphotos.com/photographer/peter-marlow/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Peter Marlow</a> (1952-2016) was known for his journalistic attention to people and happenings in conflict zones and political interactions. Throughout his career, though, he also embarked on numerous personal documentary projects like <em>Liverpool: Looking Out to Sea, </em>which he completed in the late 1980s and early 1990s as the city experienced sharp economic decline—its historic docks were no longer viable for global industry. He was also president of <a href="https://www.magnumphotos.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Magnum Photos</a> twice.</p>



<p>One of Marlow&#8217;s more meditative projects revolved around 42 Anglican cathedrals across England. The Anglican Christian tradition stems from the establishment of the Church of England following the <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_Reformation" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">English Reformation</a> in the 16th century, although the cathedrals&#8217; architectural lineage usually predates this period. </p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2537" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-6.jpg" alt="a photograph of the nave of a cathedral in natural light" class="wp-image-475882" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-6-640x812.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-6-960x1218.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-6-768x974.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-6-1211x1536.jpg 1211w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-6-1615x2048.jpg 1615w" sizes="(max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Worcester Cathedral (2010)</figcaption></figure>



<p>Completing <em>The English Cathedral</em> involved coordinating visits at times of day when Marlow could experience the buildings in natural light, not unlike the way they were seen for centuries before the advent of electricity. He focused on the churches&#8217; naves, illuminating their rosette-covered wooden ceilings, Gothic arches, altars, and hints of apses beyond.</p>



<p>An exhibition of <em>The English Cathedral</em> opens on July 21 and continues through August 31 at <a href="https://cathedral.southwark.anglican.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Southwark Cathedral</a>, which has roots dating back at least to the 11th century. Today, it&#8217;s the oldest Gothic church in London.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" width="2000" height="2537" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-3.jpg" alt="a photograph of the nave of a cathedral in natural light" class="wp-image-475879" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-3-640x812.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-3-960x1218.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-3-768x974.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-3-1211x1536.jpg 1211w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-3-1615x2048.jpg 1615w" sizes="(max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Peterborough Cathedral (2010)</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" width="2000" height="2537" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-5.jpg" alt="a photograph of the nave of a cathedral in natural light" class="wp-image-475881" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-5.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-5-640x812.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-5-960x1218.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-5-768x974.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-5-1211x1536.jpg 1211w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-5-1615x2048.jpg 1615w" sizes="(max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Southwark Cathedral (2010)</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2537" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-1.jpg" alt="a photograph of the nave of a cathedral in natural light" class="wp-image-475884" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-1.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-1-640x812.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-1-960x1218.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-1-768x974.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-1-1211x1536.jpg 1211w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-1-1615x2048.jpg 1615w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Derby Cathedral (2010)</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2537" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-6.jpg" alt="a photograph of the nave of a cathedral in natural light" class="wp-image-475882" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-6-640x812.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-6-960x1218.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-6-768x974.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-6-1211x1536.jpg 1211w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/marlow-6-1615x2048.jpg 1615w" sizes="(max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Worcester Cathedral (2010)</figcaption></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Experience Ana Mendieta&#8217;s Visceral, &#8216;Neolithic&#8217; Work in a Major Survey</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/ana-mendieta-exhibition-photography-sculpture-art-history/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Wed, 15 Jul 2026 14:12:43 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Nature]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Photography]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Ana Mendieta]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[art history]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[environment]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[feminism]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[land art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[self-portrait]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=475866</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-7.jpg" alt="Experience Ana Mendieta&#8217;s Visceral, &#8216;Neolithic&#8217; Work in a Major Survey" />A large-scale, immersive exhibition of her work opens today at Tate Modern.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/ana-mendieta-exhibition-photography-sculpture-art-history/">Experience Ana Mendieta&#8217;s Visceral, &#8216;Neolithic&#8217; Work in a Major Survey</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-7.jpg" alt="Experience Ana Mendieta&#8217;s Visceral, &#8216;Neolithic&#8217; Work in a Major Survey" />


<p>Rarely do artists conceive of work that is prescient and, decades on, more urgent than when it was created. One who has accomplished this is certainly <a href="https://www.anamendietaartist.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Ana Mendieta</a> (1948-1985), whose interdisciplinary practice merged photography, land art, sculpture, film, and more. And in a large-scale, immersive survey of her work that opens today at <a href="https://www.tate.org.uk/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Tate Modern</a>, more than 120 pieces revisit the groundbreaking artist&#8217;s key series and empathetic exchange with land and nature.</p>



<p>Mendieta is best known for her <em>Silueta Series</em>, in which she impressed the shape of the human body in water, mud, rock, and forests. These sometimes consisted of outlines &#8220;drawn&#8221; onto surfaces, such as a gunpowder tribute on a fallen tree, which exists eternally half-ablaze in a photograph. Others are impressed directly into the earth, as if a person had been lying there for millennia as the desert or stone formed around her.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="960" height="1444" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-2-960x1444.jpg" alt="a photographic artwork by Ana Mendieta documenting herself in the nude, laying in a rocky niche covered in flowering grasses" class="wp-image-475873" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-2-960x1444.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-2-640x963.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-2-768x1155.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-2-1021x1536.jpg 1021w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-2-1361x2048.jpg 1361w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-2.jpg 2000w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 960px) 100vw, 960px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Imágen de Yágul&#8221; (1973). © The Estate of Ana Mendieta Collection, LLC. Licensed by Artist Rights Society (ARS), New York / DACS, 2026. Courtesy of Marian Goodman Gallery and Alison Jacques, London</figcaption></figure>



<p>In what she described as &#8220;earth-body&#8221; works, Mendieta explored vital relationships between humans and nature, absence and presence, experience and temporality, and place and identity. She often turned the lens on herself, building compositions that plumb the tensions between beauty, ruggedness, vulnerability, and strength. Her practice can easily be viewed through the lens of <a href="https://www.britannica.com/topic/ecofeminism" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">ecofeminism</a>, a movement that emerged around the same time Mendieta was working, but it is also profoundly personal.</p>



<p>At 12 years old, Mendieta was separated from her parents and brother, who remained in her home country of Cuba, when she and her sister were exiled to the U.S. following the Cuban Revolution in 1959. Throughout her <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/artanddesign/2013/sep/22/ana-mendieta-artist-work-foretold-death">life and brief career</a>, she grappled with themes of displacement and disconnection. &#8220;My art is the way I reestablish the bonds that unite me to the Universe,&#8221; Mendieta said. &#8220;It is a return to the maternal source.”</p>



<p>There is also humor in her approach to self-representation, such as her early series of self-portraits in which she documented her wet hair in wild, sculptural forms or produced a sequential series of images in which an arrangement of flowers gradually conceals her face. Within a few years, the work adopted a more solemn, enigmatic tone, characterized by voids, organic forms, gesture, and ephemerality.</p>



<p>Mendieta also drew on her fascination with archaeology to create multimedia works that delved into the relationship between humans and the land. &#8220;My work is basically in the tradition of a Neolithic art,&#8221; she said in 1984. &#8220;I’m not interested in the formal qualities of my materials, but their emotional and sensual ones.&#8221;</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2700" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-11.jpeg" alt="a woman stands in front of a black-and-white photographic artwork of carved earth with an abstract human form" class="wp-image-475877" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-11.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-11-640x864.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-11-960x1296.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-11-768x1037.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-11-1138x1536.jpeg 1138w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-11-1517x2048.jpeg 1517w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;La Vivificación de la Carne: El Laberinto de Venus Series (The Vivification of the Flesh: Labyrinth of Venus Series)&#8221; (1982), installation view at Tate Modern, 2026. Artwork © The Estate of Ana Mendieta Collection, LLC. Licensed by Artist Rights Society (ARS), New York / DACS 2026. Photo © Tate (Yilli Liu)</figcaption></figure>



<p>The artist&#8217;s interest in the ancient past ultimately lends a timelessness to themes that resonate through her personal narrative but also, incidentally, the ills of the present. One might think of our screen-fueled social discord and the accelerating climate crisis, both also defined by a sense of alienation and disjointedness. Though Mendieta couldn&#8217;t have conceived of these things as we experience them today, she nevertheless tapped into a kind of visceral biophilia that&#8217;s more critical than ever. The exhibition at Tate highlights not only the artist&#8217;s the desire to connect with nature but also casts a light on how far removed from it most of us have become.</p>



<p><em>Ana Mendieta </em>continues through January 17, 2027, in London. Plan your visit on Tate&#8217;s <a href="https://www.tate.org.uk/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">website</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="3000" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-9.jpg" alt="a photographic artwork by Ana Mendieta documenting an area of earth that has been carved into the form of a figure with arms outstretched, filled with bright red powder" class="wp-image-475871" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-9.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-9-640x960.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-9-960x1440.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-9-768x1152.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-9-1024x1536.jpg 1024w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-9-1365x2048.jpg 1365w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Untitled: Silueta Series&#8221; (1976). © The Estate of Ana Mendieta Collection, LLC. Licensed by Artist Rights Society (ARS), New York / DACS, 2026. Courtesy of Marian Goodman Gallery and Alison Jacques, London</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1890" height="2770" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-8.jpg" alt="a small artwork by Ana Mendieta of a simplified figure incised into a dried leaf" class="wp-image-475870" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-8.jpg 1890w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-8-640x938.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-8-960x1407.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-8-768x1126.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-8-1048x1536.jpg 1048w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-8-1397x2048.jpg 1397w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1890px) 100vw, 1890px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Untitled&#8221; (c.1984). © The Estate of Ana Mendieta Collection, LLC. Licensed by Artist Rights Society (ARS), New York / DACS, 2026. Courtesy of Marian Goodman Gallery and Alison Jacques, London</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1070" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-6.jpg" alt="a series of six black-and-white photographs of Ana Mendieta arranging flowers around her face" class="wp-image-475868" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-6-640x342.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-6-960x514.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-6-768x411.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-6-1536x822.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Untitled&#8221; (1973). © The Estate of Ana Mendieta Collection, LLC. Licensed by Artist Rights Society (ARS), New York / DACS, 2026. Courtesy of Marian Goodman Gallery and Alison Jacques, London</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1334" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-10.jpeg" alt="a figure stands in a darkened exhibition space with four projection screens showing images from film artworks by Ana Mendieta" class="wp-image-475876" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-10.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-10-640x427.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-10-960x640.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-10-768x512.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-10-1536x1025.jpeg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8216;Ana Mendieta&#8217; installation view at Tate Modern, 2026. Artworks © The Estate of Ana Mendieta Collection, LLC. Licensed by Artist Rights Society (ARS), New York / DACS 2026. Photo © Tate (Yili Liu)</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1558" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-5.jpg" alt="a series of four self-portrait photographs of Ana Mendieta with wet hair that she has formed into sculptural shapes around her face" class="wp-image-475867" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-5.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-5-640x499.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-5-960x748.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-5-768x598.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-5-1536x1197.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Untitled&#8221; (1972). © The Estate of Ana Mendieta Collection, LLC. Licensed by Artist Rights Society (ARS), New York / DACS, 2026. Courtesy of Marian Goodman Gallery and Alison Jacques, London</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2727" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-4.jpg" alt="a black-and-white photograph of a carved earth artwork by Ana Mendieta resembling a figure" class="wp-image-475875" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-4-640x873.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-4-960x1309.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-4-768x1047.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-4-1127x1536.jpg 1127w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-4-1502x2048.jpg 1502w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Untitled (Guanaroca [First Woman])&#8221; (1981). © The Estate of Ana Mendieta Collection, LLC. Licensed by Artist Rights Society (ARS), New York / DACS, 2026 / Courtesy of Marian Goodman Gallery and Alison Jacques, London</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1499" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-3.jpg" alt="an artwork by Ana Mendieta comprising black soot or earth on the ground in the shape of a figuring lying down with arms out around their head, lined with black, burning candles" class="wp-image-475874" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-3-640x480.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-3-960x720.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-3-768x576.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/mendieta-3-1536x1151.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Ñañigo Burial&#8221; (1976). © The Estate of Ana Mendieta Collection, LLC. Licensed by Artist Rights Society (ARS), New York / DACS, 2026. Courtesy of Marian Goodman Gallery and Alison Jacques, London. Photo Alex Yudzon</figcaption></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Divine Sculptures Revere a Yorùbá Goddess in Nigeria&#8217;s Ọṣun-Òṣogbo Sacred Grove</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/osun-osogbo-sacred-grove-nigeria-documentary/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Grace Ebert]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Tue, 14 Jul 2026 19:35:41 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Design]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Film]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[History]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Africa]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[architecture]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[art environments]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[documentary]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[religion]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[short film]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[spirituality]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[video]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=475855</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/osun-2.jpg" alt="Divine Sculptures Revere a Yorùbá Goddess in Nigeria&#8217;s Ọṣun-Òṣogbo Sacred Grove" />A short documentary visits the sacred art environment in southwestern Nigeria.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/osun-osogbo-sacred-grove-nigeria-documentary/">Divine Sculptures Revere a Yorùbá Goddess in Nigeria&#8217;s Ọṣun-Òṣogbo Sacred Grove</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/osun-2.jpg" alt="Divine Sculptures Revere a Yorùbá Goddess in Nigeria&#8217;s Ọṣun-Òṣogbo Sacred Grove" />


<p>In Yorùbá culture, it&#8217;s said that more than 600 years ago, a hunter discovered a lush grove in southwestern Nigeria carved by a rushing river. His community had experienced drought and eagerly moved to the region, which they quickly learned was under the rule of the goddess of rivers and fertility, Ọ̀ṣun. In exchange for protection and prosperity, the people promised to celebrate the deity, and this pact grounds what&#8217;s now known as the Ọṣun-Òṣogbo Sacred Grove. </p>



<p><a href="https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1118/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">A UNESCO World Heritage site</a> spanning 190 acres, the spiritual sanctuary has long been revered by the Yorùbá people, and in the mid-20th century, a group of artists revitalized the landscape by erecting large-scale sculptures in honor of its namesake. Dubbed the New Sacred Art Movement, the efforts are the subject of <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I4m6Uuckfp4&amp;t=704s">a short documentary</a> released by The Met that visits the grove and highlights some of the artists who&#8217;ve carved totems, shaped enormous creatures from clay and mud, and established a vibrant art environment to be passed down through generations.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-embed is-type-video is-provider-youtube wp-block-embed-youtube wp-embed-aspect-16-9 wp-has-aspect-ratio"><div class="wp-block-embed__wrapper">
<iframe loading="lazy" title="Ọṣun-Òṣogbo Sacred Grove, Nigeria | Africa’s Cultural Landmarks" width="500" height="281" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/I4m6Uuckfp4?start=704&#038;feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>
</div></figure>



<p>Directed by Sosena Solomon, the film is part of The Met&#8217;s series devoted to Africa&#8217;s cultural landmarks, made in collaboration with the World Monuments Fund. It highlights some of the makers creating and repairing works, including Kasali Akangbe Ogun, who helped lead the New Sacred Art Movement alongside Austrian-Nigerian artist Susanne Wenger and Chief Adebisi Akanji in the 1960s. Today, he continues to carve totemic shrines and share his craft with his children.</p>



<p>While many similar sites fell into disrepair, the artists who worked in the grove helped to safeguard its sacredness as they built an expansive art environment visualizing various deities. An annual festival and pilgrimages attract visitors each year, and as generations pass, artists and caretakers are working to both preserve what&#8217;s been built and also pass down knowledge to ensure the space&#8217;s survival. &#8220;What makes Ọṣun-Òṣogbo such a special place is,&#8221; says Chief Nike Davies-Okundaye, &#8220;this is a living story.&#8221;</p>



<p>Ọṣun-Òṣogbo Sacred Grove is one of 13 cultural sites The Met visited across the continent, and you can find more on <a href="https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PL8HAkqKX065DuxC3u74dgq_81EvSNU5Sq&amp;si=EunXzTQ6Xvg39shK" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">YouTube</a>. You might also enjoy <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2024/07/sacred-sites-library-of-esoterica/">this book</a> surveying more than 400 spiritual environments around the world.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="960" height="549" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/osun-1-960x549.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-475857" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/osun-1-960x549.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/osun-1-640x366.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/osun-1-768x439.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/osun-1-1536x879.jpg 1536w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/osun-1.jpg 2000w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 960px) 100vw, 960px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="960" height="524" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/osun-3-960x524.jpg" alt="a screen grab of the spiritual sculptures of the yoruba grove" class="wp-image-475859" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/osun-3-960x524.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/osun-3-640x349.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/osun-3-768x419.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/osun-3-1536x839.jpg 1536w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/osun-3.jpg 2000w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 960px) 100vw, 960px" /></figure>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. 		<item>
		<title>&#8216;Absurdist Basketmaker&#8217; Lewis Prosser Weaves Contemporary Visions of Regional Heritage</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/lewis-prosser-baskets-costumes-folklore-performance/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Tue, 14 Jul 2026 14:27:32 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Craft]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[History]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[baskets]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[costumes]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[England]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[folk art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[folklore]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Lewis Prosser]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[masks]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[performance]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[performance art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[public art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Wales]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=475837</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-2-e1784033531178.jpg" alt="&#8216;Absurdist Basketmaker&#8217; Lewis Prosser Weaves Contemporary Visions of Regional Heritage" />The Cardiff-based artist taps into storytelling, masking traditions, and public ceremony and celebration.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/lewis-prosser-baskets-costumes-folklore-performance/">&#8216;Absurdist Basketmaker&#8217; Lewis Prosser Weaves Contemporary Visions of Regional Heritage</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-2-e1784033531178.jpg" alt="&#8216;Absurdist Basketmaker&#8217; Lewis Prosser Weaves Contemporary Visions of Regional Heritage" />


<p>During the medieval and Renaissance periods, baskets were everyday essentials—no plastic bags at the supermarket or even reusable totes. They were also used for all sorts of activities, from handled varieties for produce at the market to decorative vessels holding sewing materials to large versions that could be worn like rucksacks. For Cardiff-based artist <a href="https://www.lewisprosser.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Lewis Prosser</a>, a self-described &#8220;absurdist basketmaker,&#8221; folklore, regional identity, and cultural heritage center a multidisciplinary practice.</p>



<p>Through sculptural baskets that can be worn as costumes or displayed like venerable sculptures, Prosser taps into storytelling, masking traditions, and public ceremony and celebration. Welsh communities still celebrate <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mari_Lwyd" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Mari Lwyd</a> during the Christmas period, a festivity that may have emerged with <a href="https://www.history.com/articles/celts" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">the Celts</a>. A small group of men bedecked in ribbons and rosettes parade around town, leading a figure wearing an eerie horse skull. Another ceremonial festival, <a href="https://earl-of-rone.org.uk/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">The Hunting of the Earl of Rone</a>, takes place annually in the village of Combe Martin, North Devon, and although updated over the centuries, is also thought to have originated in pre-Christian times.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1331" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-5.jpg" alt="a documentary photo of a performance featuring people wearing masks and abstract costumes made from woven baskets" class="wp-image-475846" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-5.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-5-640x426.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-5-960x639.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-5-768x511.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-5-1536x1022.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8216;Making Merrie.&#8217; Photo by Kristen McTernan</figcaption></figure>



<p>In projects like <em>Making Merrie, </em>Prosser combines music and dance in an ode to British and Irish folk performances called mummers&#8217; plays, which were often staged during holidays and typically feature combat between two opposing forces, such as good and evil or winter and spring.</p>



<p>Prosser created the wicker costumes using basketry techniques found in Wales and southwestern England, invoking the craft as &#8220;an essential human skill we’re at risk of forgetting—a skill that, if lost, means losing part of what it is to be human,&#8221; he says in a statement. The costumes are now in the collection of the <a href="https://www.instagram.com/folk.preservation.society/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Folk Preservation Society</a> in Teignmouth, Devon, which continues to activate them in performances from time to time.</p>



<p>Currently, Prosser is facilitating a collaborative project called <em>The Baskets Between Carnival and Lent. </em>Inspired by Pieter Breughel the Elder&#8217;s seminal painting &#8220;<a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fight_Between_Carnival_and_Lent" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">The Fight Between Carnival and Lent</a>&#8221; (1559), Prosser takes the composition&#8217;s 24 woven objects as a starting point, including willow shutters on buildings, a birdcage, and a woven beehive, otherwise known as a skep. Prosser is joining 10 basketmakers from across Europe to recreate all two dozen in the painting, and the finished pieces are slated for a show at <a href="https://www.orielmyrddingallery.co.uk/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Oriel Myrddin Gallery</a> in Carmarthen, Wales, in spring 2027.</p>



<p>Prosser is also working toward a new performance for <a href="https://www.cajadeburgos.com/bienalburgos/artistas/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Burgos Biennial 2026</a> in Burgos, Spain, which kicks off in late September. &#8220;For this project, I will be devising an elaborate new basket-based sport called &#8216;hornball&#8217; (<em>cuerno pelota</em>): a combination of ritual harvest celebration, competitive ball games, and wearable sculptures,&#8221; Prosser tells Colossal. See more on his <a href="https://www.instagram.com/clovisvosser" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1428" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-9.jpg" alt="a documentary photo of a performance outdoors featuring people wearing masks and abstract costumes made from woven baskets" class="wp-image-475844" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-9.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-9-640x457.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-9-960x685.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-9-768x548.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-9-1536x1097.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="3000" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-4.jpg" alt="a documentary photo of a performance featuring a figure wearing an abstract costume made from woven basketry" class="wp-image-475841" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-4-640x960.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-4-960x1440.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-4-768x1152.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-4-1024x1536.jpg 1024w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-4-1365x2048.jpg 1365w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-1.jpg" alt="a documentary photo of a performance featuring people wearing masks and abstract costumes made from woven baskets" class="wp-image-475838" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-1.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-1-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-1-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-1-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-1-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="3000" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-3.jpg" alt="a documentary photo of a performance featuring a figure wearing an abstract costume made from woven basketry" class="wp-image-475840" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-3-640x960.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-3-960x1440.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-3-768x1152.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-3-1024x1536.jpg 1024w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-3-1365x2048.jpg 1365w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1200" height="800" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-7.jpeg" alt="a documentary photo of a public art performance featuring a mask-like basket sculpture tied with numerous ribbons being rolled around on the pavement by a man as onlookers watch" class="wp-image-475842" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-7.jpeg 1200w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-7-640x427.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-7-960x640.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/prosser-7-768x512.jpeg 768w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1200px) 100vw, 1200px" /></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Korea&#8217;s Coastal Folklore Surfaces in Jeongmin Lee&#8217;s Ink Illustrations</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/jeongmin-lee-korean-folklore-illustrations/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Grace Ebert]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Mon, 13 Jul 2026 18:30:00 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Illustration]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[ink]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Jeongmin Lee]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[narrative]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[South Korea]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=475797</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-10.jpg" alt="Korea&#8217;s Coastal Folklore Surfaces in Jeongmin Lee&#8217;s Ink Illustrations" />"I rarely paint a folktale exactly as it's written," Lee says. "I'm more interested in its symbols, emotions, and the questions it leaves behind."</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/jeongmin-lee-korean-folklore-illustrations/">Korea&#8217;s Coastal Folklore Surfaces in Jeongmin Lee&#8217;s Ink Illustrations</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-10.jpg" alt="Korea&#8217;s Coastal Folklore Surfaces in Jeongmin Lee&#8217;s Ink Illustrations" />


<p><a href="https://mintheelephant.com/work" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Jeongmin Lee</a> is interested in the ways &#8220;memory is carried through craft and repetition.&#8221; On traditional Korean mulberry paper, or <em>hanji</em>, Lee draws delicate lines in ink and pigments known as <em>bunchae</em>, rendering rippling textures that whirl across the page. Steeped in local folklore and mythology, the Busan-based artist creates surreal scenes that conjure fantastical tales of life by the sea.</p>



<p>&#8220;Most of my recent projects begin with reading regional folktales, visiting places connected to those stories, and collecting fragments of history, mythology, and oral traditions,&#8221; she says. &#8220;I rarely paint a folktale exactly as it&#8217;s written; I&#8217;m more interested in its symbols, emotions, and the questions it leaves behind.&#8221;</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2828" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-7.jpeg" alt="a surreal illustration of a nude woman standing atop circular forms" class="wp-image-475823" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-7.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-7-640x905.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-7-960x1357.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-7-768x1086.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-7-1086x1536.jpeg 1086w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-7-1448x2048.jpeg 1448w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<p>Many of Lee&#8217;s compositions focus on women&#8217;s knowledge, labor, and resilience and how those qualities emerge through coastal storytelling. Tales of <a href="https://folkency.nfm.go.kr/topic/detail/2790" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">powerful sea gods</a> and the diving traditions of <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2020/07/hyung-s-kim-haenyeo/">the haenyeo</a> commingle into balanced illustrations that translate the symbols and motifs of the region anew.</p>



<p>While her approach is labor-intensive, Lee enjoys utilizing such a meticulous, meditative technique. &#8220;Painting with traditional pigments requires a slow, layered process. The colors are built gradually, allowing the paper and pigments to create subtle textures that wouldn&#8217;t be possible with other materials,&#8221; she adds. &#8220;It gives me space to sit with these stories while I paint them.</p>



<p>Many of the works shown here are part of <em>Daughters of the Sea(s)</em>, an ongoing series on view alongside artist <a href="https://heykato.studio/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Kato Trofimova</a> for the <a href="https://sabrs.lv/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">SĀBRS Festival</a> in Riga. Lee hopes to expand the project into one that&#8217;s participatory and connects similar narratives from across the globe. &#8220;I&#8217;m exploring ways that folklore can become something people experience and talk about together, rather than something that exists only on a gallery wall,&#8221; Lee shares.</p>



<p>She&#8217;s also currently working on a graphic novel centering on Busan&#8217;s mythology and folklore, which she hopes to complete next year. Keep up with her projects on <a href="https://www.instagram.com/mintheelephant" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2828" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-11.jpg" alt="a surreal illustration of two abstract figures facing each other and then waves on the bottom" class="wp-image-475816" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-11.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-11-640x905.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-11-960x1357.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-11-768x1086.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-11-1086x1536.jpg 1086w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-11-1448x2048.jpg 1448w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>

<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2828" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-12.jpg" alt="a surreal illustration of a woman surrounded by waves" class="wp-image-475817" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-12.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-12-640x905.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-12-960x1357.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-12-768x1086.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-12-1086x1536.jpg 1086w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lee-12-1448x2048.jpg 1448w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Helena Minginowicz Transforms Humble Paper Towel into Ethereal Paintings</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/helena-minginowicz-paper-towel-renaissance-paintings-value/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Mon, 13 Jul 2026 17:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[art history]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Helena Minginowicz]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[painting]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[paper]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=475798</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-7-e1783955577732.jpeg" alt="Helena Minginowicz Transforms Humble Paper Towel into Ethereal Paintings" />"Civilizations are remembered through their monuments, but understood through the things they throw away," the artist says.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/helena-minginowicz-paper-towel-renaissance-paintings-value/">Helena Minginowicz Transforms Humble Paper Towel into Ethereal Paintings</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-7-e1783955577732.jpeg" alt="Helena Minginowicz Transforms Humble Paper Towel into Ethereal Paintings" />


<p>&#8220;Civilizations are remembered through their monuments, but understood through the things they throw away,&#8221; says artist <a href="https://www.instagram.com/santa___helena/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Helena Minginowicz</a>, whose sensitive paintings interrogate our understanding of value. Using airbrushed acrylic, which can be built up in lightweight, translucent layers, the artist takes one of the most quotidian household items as a starting point: paper towel.</p>



<p>With its machine-embossed, moisture-wicking patterns, the absorbent paper comprises an instantly recognizable substrate. The precise, textured flourishes are aesthetically pleasing, and yet it&#8217;s hard to completely separate them from our associations with mass-produced paper products that are designed for one-time use and disposability. This dichotomy sits at he heart of Minginowicz&#8217;s practice, in which she explores &#8220;how changing the hierarchy of materials can reshape the way we perceive value, dignity, and the human experience,&#8221; she tells Colossal.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1857" height="1093" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-9-e1783951983777.jpeg" alt="a painting of a woman's face, inspired by a Renaissance portrait, on two sheets of paper towel" class="wp-image-475804" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-9-e1783951983777.jpeg 1857w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-9-e1783951983777-640x377.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-9-e1783951983777-960x565.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-9-e1783951983777-768x452.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-9-e1783951983777-1536x904.jpeg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1857px) 100vw, 1857px" /></figure>



<p>Minginowicz&#8217;s embossed pieces from everyday domestic material are one facet of a broader multimedia approach to materiality in which she creates paintings on canvas and also painstakingly embosses delicate tissues. The paper towel works, in addition to some that are made on supermarket-style plastic bags, are then presented between thick slabs of acrylic, transforming them into objects with substantial heft and dimensionality.</p>



<p>&#8220;Every civilization constructs its own hierarchy of values,&#8221; the artist says. &#8220;It decides what deserves to be preserved, admired, and passed on to future generations. Monuments, works of art, symbols, and myths preserve an image of humanity as we wish to remember it—strong, beautiful, enduring, and heroic. Yet every monument has its reverse.&#8221;</p>



<p>Minginowicz&#8217; imagery draws on the style of <a href="/tags/renaissance">Renaissance</a> paintings, especially focusing on expressiveness, intimacy, and the idealized female figure. One might think of Sandro Botticelli&#8217;s &#8220;The Birth of Venus&#8221; or aristocratic <a href="https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/portraiture-in-renaissance-and-baroque-europe" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">portraiture</a> of the era. &#8220;For centuries, painting monumentalized what civilizations wished to remember: saints, heroes, gods, victories, myths, and ideals. I use that same language to ask a different question: Who deserves to be remembered with dignity? Not only heroes. Not only the victorious. But every human being.&#8221;</p>



<p>Minginowicz is currently working toward a solo exhibition at <a href="https://galerieprima.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Galerie Prima</a> in Paris, which is slated to open on October 8. Follow updates and see more on <a href="https://www.instagram.com/santa___helena/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2169" height="2040" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-3.jpeg" alt="a painting of a man's face with a mark in the shape of a rabbit on his cheek, inspired by a Renaissance portrait, on a torn sheet of paper towel" class="wp-image-475801" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-3.jpeg 2169w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-3-640x602.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-3-960x903.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-3-768x722.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-3-1536x1445.jpeg 1536w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-3-2048x1926.jpeg 2048w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2169px) 100vw, 2169px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2238" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-2.jpeg" alt="a painting of a man's face with a mark in the shape of a rabbit on his cheek, inspired by a Renaissance portrait, on a sheet of paper towel that is encased between two thick pieces of acrylic" class="wp-image-475800" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-2.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-2-640x716.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-2-960x1074.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-2-768x859.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-2-1373x1536.jpeg 1373w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-2-1830x2048.jpeg 1830w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1159" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-11.jpeg" alt="two small painted female figures inspired by classical paintings on two sheets of paper towel" class="wp-image-475809" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-11.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-11-640x371.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-11-960x556.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-11-768x445.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-11-1536x890.jpeg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2215" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-5.jpeg" alt="a painting of a hand and breast from a Renaissance painting on on paper towel" class="wp-image-475806" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-5.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-5-640x709.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-5-960x1063.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-5-768x851.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-5-1387x1536.jpeg 1387w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-5-1849x2048.jpeg 1849w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1167" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-6.jpeg" alt="a painting of two figures from a Renaissance painting on two sheets of paper towel" class="wp-image-475807" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-6.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-6-640x373.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-6-960x560.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-6-768x448.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/minginowicz-6-1536x896.jpeg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Uncanny Landscapes in Pen and Ink Span Wooden Panels by John Buck</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/john-buck-wooden-panel-pink-ink-drawings/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Mon, 13 Jul 2026 14:23:53 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[drawing]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[ink]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[John Buck]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[landscapes]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[pen]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[wood]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=475787</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-7.jpg" alt="Uncanny Landscapes in Pen and Ink Span Wooden Panels by John Buck" />The Bozeman-based artist is known for his eccentric wooden works that draw on folklore, personal memory, and daily observations.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/john-buck-wooden-panel-pink-ink-drawings/">Uncanny Landscapes in Pen and Ink Span Wooden Panels by John Buck</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-7.jpg" alt="Uncanny Landscapes in Pen and Ink Span Wooden Panels by John Buck" />


<p>From the Three Patriarchs of Zion Canyon to the swamps of Louisiana to the immense cascade of Niagara Falls, <a href="https://www.johnbuckart.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">John Buck</a>’s landscapes evoke the juxtapositions and proportions of dreams. His solo exhibition, <em>Mont Blanc on Wood</em> at <a href="https://www.zollaliebermangallery.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Zolla / Lieberman Gallery</a>, draws us to the fuzzy boundary between the familiar and the uncanny.</p>



<p>The Bozeman-based artist is known for his eccentric, often life-size wooden sculptures that draw on folklore, personal memory, and daily observations. Figures are sometimes hybridized with other objects, and idiosyncratic drawings on wood panel reveal expansive landscapes populated by anthropomorphized plants and dramatic rock pinnacles.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1473" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-5.jpg" alt="a pen-and-ink drawing on a wooden surface of a rocky desert area with a small lake in the middle, in the center of which a lighthouse sits" class="wp-image-475794" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-5.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-5-640x471.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-5-960x707.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-5-768x566.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-5-1536x1131.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Lighthouse&#8221; (2024), pen and ink on wood, 27 x 36 ½ inches</figcaption></figure>



<p>The works in <em>Mont Blanc on Wood </em>span a range of places and references, emphasizing landscapes where things feel perhaps a little &#8220;off.&#8221; The desert stares back in &#8220;Cactus Grove (No. 13),&#8221; and in &#8220;Lighthouse (No. 18),&#8221; a light station in the middle of a desert lake shines mostly onto arid, rocky landforms.</p>



<p>&#8220;Buck reflects on social and political realities, environmental concerns, and the eccentricities of human behavior, all while maintaining a sense of humor and a deep engagement with craft,&#8221; the gallery says. &#8220;His art balances storytelling with formal clarity, inviting viewers into a world where the familiar becomes speculative and symbolic.&#8221;</p>



<p><em>Mont Blanc on Wood </em>continues through August 8 in Chicago.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2721" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-4.jpg" alt="a pen-and-ink drawing on a wooden surface featuring various kinds of cartoonish cacti with eyes" class="wp-image-475793" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-4-640x871.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-4-960x1306.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-4-768x1045.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-4-1129x1536.jpg 1129w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-4-1505x2048.jpg 1505w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Cactus Grove&#8221; (2024), pen and ink on wood, 36 ½ x 27 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1666" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-9.jpg" alt="a pen-and-ink drawing on a wooden surface featuring the three &quot;patriarchs&quot; in Zion Canyon, Utah" class="wp-image-475796" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-9.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-9-640x533.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-9-960x800.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-9-768x640.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-9-1536x1279.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Three Patriarchs, Utah&#8221; (2024), pen and ink on wood, 26 ½ x 31 ½ inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1613" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-6.jpg" alt="a pen-and-ink drawing on a wooden surface of factories foregrounded by turbulent waters" class="wp-image-475795" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-6-640x516.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-6-960x774.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-6-768x619.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-6-1536x1239.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;The Never Sweat Mine&#8221; (2024), pen and ink on wood, 21 ¼ x 26 ½ inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1651" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-3.jpg" alt="a pen-and-ink drawing on a wooden surface featuring a swamp setting with trees and stumps" class="wp-image-475792" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-3-640x528.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-3-960x792.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-3-768x634.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-3-1536x1268.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Atchafalaya&#8221; (2024), pen and ink on wood, 26 ½ x 32 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2763" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-1.jpg" alt="a pen-and-ink drawing on a wooden surface featuring waterfalls amid mountains" class="wp-image-475790" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-1.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-1-640x884.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-1-960x1326.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-1-768x1061.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-1-1112x1536.jpg 1112w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/buck-1-1482x2048.jpg 1482w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;7 Waterfalls (No14),&#8221; (2024), pen and ink on wood, 37 x 27 inches</figcaption></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Andrew Salgado&#8217;s Gestural Still Lifes Pulse with Energy</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/andrew-salgado-flower-still-life-paintings/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Grace Ebert]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Sat, 11 Jul 2026 17:46:42 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Andrew Salgado]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[flowers]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[literature]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[painting]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[still life]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=475772</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-7.jpg" alt="Andrew Salgado&#8217;s Gestural Still Lifes Pulse with Energy" />Color ripples across each canvas, presenting the stylized florals in various states of blossom and decay.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/andrew-salgado-flower-still-life-paintings/">Andrew Salgado&#8217;s Gestural Still Lifes Pulse with Energy</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-7.jpg" alt="Andrew Salgado&#8217;s Gestural Still Lifes Pulse with Energy" />


<p>A largely figurative painter with a penchant for literary citation, <a href="https://andrewsalgado.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Andrew Salgado</a> turns his attention to the still life in a new body of work. Wanting to depart from <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/tags/andrew-salgado/">his narrative-driven process</a> in favor of subject matter allowing for greater intuition and spontaneity, the artist began to render vibrant bouquets in his signature gestural marks. Color ripples across each canvas, presenting the stylized florals in various states of blossom and decay.</p>



<p>Salgado is an avid, eclectic reader, and while his still lifes operate at a remove from his typically reference-rich compositions, they still contain snippets of texts and art history. Awash in blues of all shades, &#8220;The Prince,&#8221; for example, emerges from <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gargoyles_(novel)" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">a Thomas Bernhard novel</a> that follows an aristocratic protagonist&#8217;s descent into paranoia and obsession. In Salgado&#8217;s painting, the singular, focused color palette and flowers splayed in every direction mirror the frenetic energy of a message left on the table.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2419" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-1.jpg" alt="a gestural still life of sun flowers in a vase rendered in bright bold colors" class="wp-image-475773" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-1.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-1-640x774.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-1-960x1161.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-1-768x929.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-1-1270x1536.jpg 1270w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-1-1693x2048.jpg 1693w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Dear Theo&#8221; (2026)</figcaption></figure>



<p>There&#8217;s also &#8220;Dear Theo,&#8221; which centers on a bright cluster of sunflowers synonymous with <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/tags/vincent-van-gogh/">Vincent van Gogh</a>. Like the title, a scribbled note at the bottom right is addressed to Theo, the Dutch painter&#8217;s brother and longtime financial supporter. &#8220;To be sufficiently heated up to melt those golds and those flower tones, not just anybody can do that,&#8221; Vincent famously wrote Theo. &#8220;It takes an individual’s whole and entire energy and attention.&#8221;</p>



<p>Being attuned to one&#8217;s energy and attention is also critical in this body of work. Rather than follow a rigid, predetermined path, the artist opted for more freedom and the ability to latch onto a thought or association and allow it, and the paint, to lead.</p>



<p><em>Glory!</em> is on view from July 16 to August 15 at <a href="https://beerslondon.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">BEERS London</a>. Keep up with Salgado on <a href="https://www.instagram.com/andrew.salgado.art/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2563" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-6.jpg" alt="a gestural still life of yellow flowers in a vase rendered in bright bold colors" class="wp-image-475778" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-6-640x820.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-6-960x1230.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-6-768x984.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-6-1199x1536.jpg 1199w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-6-1598x2048.jpg 1598w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Narcissus Wept&#8221; (2026)</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2008" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-5.jpg" alt="a gestural still life of blue flowers in a vase rendered in bright bold colors" class="wp-image-475777" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-5.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-5-640x643.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-5-960x964.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-5-150x150.jpg 150w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-5-768x771.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-5-1530x1536.jpg 1530w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;The Prince&#8221; (2026)</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2514" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-4.jpg" alt="a gestural still life of flowers in a vase rendered in bright bold colors" class="wp-image-475776" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-4-640x804.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-4-960x1207.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-4-768x965.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-4-1222x1536.jpg 1222w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/salgado-4-1629x2048.jpg 1629w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;For Myra&#8221; (2026)</figcaption></figure>
